audit.title: Call Multiple Data Sources

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a self-contained purpose statement — "This tutorial shows you how make multiple API calls…" (with a typo). Section leads are mostly independent, but the `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` section is empty, so a lifted chunk under that heading yields nothing.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1→H4 hierarchy, 0 level skips, 46 bullets. Weakened by 0 tables (the API price-path mapping is a natural table) and one 647-word section.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong real numbers — `0.25590956997723491 LINK`, `1.104471544715335 LINK`, median `66822.81`, addresses, slot/expiration params. Measured facts flag "0 with units" and vague quantifier "many," but the numeric density is good for a tutorial.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 21 external links, 7 to primary sources (GitHub, Remix), inline links to API docs and Node.js references. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Tutorial prose lacks a crisp, liftable one-sentence definition of the core operation (making/aggregating multiple DON HTTP requests). Key terms (`donId`, `slotIdNumber`) are described inline but not defined quotably.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. This is the largest scored deficit; note the served `.md` may strip head metadata (CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm).

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 8 fenced blocks, all tagged, expected console output shown, `REPLACE` placeholders clear. But `source.js` and the Solidity contract are only linked, not shown inline — an agent reading this page alone cannot reconstruct the full example.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the "how do I call multiple APIs" intent and prerequisites, but no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased headings (e.g., simulation errors, secrets-upload failures).

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Generally clear; minor errors — "how make", "you can read the API docs… calculate" (agreement), inconsistent "Coinpaprika/CoinPaprika" capitalization, stray capitalized "These arguments".

audit.summary: This is a solid, link-rich Chainlink Functions tutorial showing how to fetch and median a `BTC/USD` price across three API providers, with a full annotated `request.js` walkthrough and real sandbox output. Its biggest strength is citation density (30 links, 7 to primary sources) and a concrete end-to-end console transcript. Its biggest weakness is an **empty `### FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` heading** (a broken, unretrievable chunk) compounded by missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates) and no symptom/troubleshooting coverage. Honest verdict: good developer docs that lose GEO points to a structural gap and absent metadata, both cheaply fixable.

recommendations.title: Fill or remove the empty `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` section
recommendations.issue: heading has zero body content — an orphan chunk.
recommendations.change: Add the contract snippet (or 2–3 sentences describing the consumer contract's `sendRequest`/`fulfillRequest` role) plus the Remix link already used later; or delete the heading.
recommendations.why: empty headings retrieve as blank chunks and waste an H3 anchor; a filled section becomes independently citable.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/troubleshooting section
recommendations.where: new `## Troubleshooting` before or after `## Examine the code`
recommendations.issue: no coverage of failure modes; devs query by error string.
recommendations.change: Add 3–5 Q-phrased entries, e.g. "Secrets uploaded but request not fulfilled", "`secp256k1 unavailable` warning", "Insufficient LINK / minimum balance error", each with the one-line fix.
recommendations.why: symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled tutorial prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.issue: measured facts show no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: ["JavaScript","Solidity"]`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line. (Confirm whether the served `.md` merely strips head — see off-page notes.)
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals make the page easier to parse and trust; largest scored gap.

recommendations.title: Convert the API price-path mapping to a table
recommendations.where: "The prices are respectively located at:" list
recommendations.issue: provider → JSON path → sample endpoint spread across prose and bullets.
recommendations.change: One table with columns Provider | Endpoint | Price JSON path | API-key required.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract per-provider facts as discrete rows; page currently has 0 tables.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical one-sentence lead to `source.js`
recommendations.issue: opens with "The Decentralized Oracle Network will run the JavaScript code" — not the how.
recommendations.change: Lead with the canonical API: "Use `Functions.makeHttpRequest` to issue each provider request, then return the median via `Functions.encodeUint256`." Name the wrong pattern explicitly (don't use `fetch`/`axios` inside the DON sandbox).
recommendations.why: puts the canonical SDK helper in the first liftable sentence, resisting generic `fetch`/`axios` priors.

recommendations.title: Fix clarity/consistency errors
recommendations.change: "how to make"; standardize "CoinPaprika"; lowercase mid-sentence "these arguments".
recommendations.why: consistent entity naming aids resolution; fluency is independently rewarded.

antiPatterns: **Orphan heading / broken chunk:** `### FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` has no content.
**Undated content:** no visible or structured last-updated signal.
**Vague quantifier:** "many different API providers" (minor; the count is 3, so state it).
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no missing code tags detected.
offPageNotes: The audited artifact is the `.md` export; head metadata "could not be verified." The CLI should pass raw `<head>` from the HTML page before concluding JSON-LD/canonical are truly absent — the deficit may be partly a served-format artifact.
`llms.txt` is already referenced inline (good site-level signal); ensure this tutorial is listed there.
Full example fidelity depends on the linked GitHub `source.js` — inlining it would reduce reliance on off-page fetch during agent runs.
